panels.title: Emitter status — read before the gates below
panels.description: Explains what feeds this board and why the thaw-warm gate stats specifically may read empty in a live env.

options.content:
This board scores resume latency off `gardenio_resume_latency_seconds`, now emitted by **two** processes: the **slack-bridge** records every non-runsc thread-agent cold resume (`path=cold`, `R0`) at first proof-of-life (task **ka-0000004119**), and the **controller** records the gVisor freeze/thaw resume (`path=thaw-warm`/`thaw-fresh`, `R4`/`R3`) — the path the **R4 sub-second gate** (p50 < 1s, p95 < 1.5s) below scores.

**Watch _Resumes observed (24h)_ on the right for overall liveness** — it should be positive whenever any thread agent has resumed. **The thaw-warm gate stats stay empty until a gVisor freeze/thaw actually fires**, which in prod is a hard-hold on the near-idle `gvisor-poc` canary — so an empty R4 gate is expected there, not an emitter bug. The alerts (`ResumeP95High`, `ResumeWarmHitRateLow`) guard on `path="thaw-warm"` volume, so they correctly do not fire with no thaw traffic.

The **Interrupt/resume plumbing** row at the bottom (C8, **ka-0000000550**) charts the previously-invisible mechanics under these latencies: warm-B claim hit/miss, prewarmed-pool assign hit/empty, coop `--resume` conversation-restore outcomes + prepare latency, and preStop salvage success/bytes.

_Cold-resume emitter: **ka-0000004119** (C7) · thaw-path guard fix: **ka-0000007439** · Epic: **ka-0000002590** (Phase 5 rapid-response thaw)._

panels.title: Resumes observed (24h)
panels.description: Total resume-latency observations recorded across all paths in the last 24h — the board's liveness signal. 0 (neutral) means the emitter has not fired a single sample yet and every gate/percentile below is awaiting its first observation, NOT reporting a healthy sub-second result. Any positive value means real data is flowing. Empty-branch liveness: the `or vector(0)` fallback is gated on `up{component="slack-bridge"} == 1` — the process that actually observes resume latency (measured: gardenio_resume_latency_seconds carries component="slack-bridge", not "agents") — so a 0 means the resume path was genuinely idle, not that its exporter went away.

panels.title: R4 (thaw-warm) p95 — gate < 1.5s
panels.description: p95 resume latency for the R4 thaw-onto-warm-placeholder path. The Phase 5 success criterion is R4 p50 < 1s and p95 < 1.5s (sub-second-resume-integration.md). Green < 1.5s, red above.

panels.title: R4 (thaw-warm) p50 — gate < 1s
panels.description: p50 resume latency for the R4 thaw-onto-warm-placeholder path. Gate: p50 < 1s. Green < 1s, red above.

panels.title: Warm-graft hit rate
panels.description: Share of thaw resumes served by a pre-Ready warm placeholder (thaw-warm) vs the total thaw volume (thaw-warm + thaw-fresh). High is good: it means the warm pool absorbed the wake instead of falling back to a fresh Pod B. Computed over a 30m window so the ratio is stable on low-traffic envs.

panels.title: Cold-fallback (thaw-fresh) count — 30m
panels.description:
Number of thaw resumes that fell back to a freshly-created Pod B (thaw-fresh, R3) in the last 30m — i.e. no warm placeholder was available. Every cold fallback is a missed warm-graft and a slower resume.

The zero is EARNED, not fabricated: it is baselined off `sum(increase(gardenio_resume_latency_seconds_count{env}[30m])) * 0`, so 0 appears only when SOME resume was observed in the same 30m window (path=thaw-fresh has never emitted — only path=cold has samples in the last 30d). With no resumes at all the tile falls through to its noValue instead of claiming a verified 0 (ka-0000006531, replaces `or vector(0)`).

defaults.noValue: no resumes observed in the last 30m — cold-fallback count UNKNOWN (not 0)

panels.title: p50 / p95 / p99 by path
panels.description: Resume-latency percentiles per path (cold | pool | thaw-fresh | thaw-warm). thaw-warm should sit well under the 1s/1.5s gate; thaw-fresh and cold ride higher. Computed from the histogram _bucket series via histogram_quantile.

panels.title: p95 by regime (R0–R4)
panels.description: p95 resume latency per cumulative benchmark regime. R0 (cold resume) is emitted live by the slack-bridge for every non-runsc thread-agent resume; the controller wake path emits R3 (thaw-fresh) and R4 (thaw-warm). R1–R2 (node-prewarm / warm-pool) are driven only by the bench harness, so they may be empty in live envs.

panels.title: p95 by role
panels.description: p95 resume latency broken out by agent role (crew/gardener/…). Surfaces whether a particular role's resume path is systematically slower.

panels.title: Resume rate by path
panels.description: Resumes per second by path. cold is the live non-runsc thread-agent resume rate (slack-bridge); the thaw-warm vs thaw-fresh split is the warm-graft hit rate over time (controller). pool appears only when the bench harness drives that regime.

panels.title: Warm-graft hit rate over time
panels.description: thaw-warm / (thaw-warm + thaw-fresh) as a 30m rolling ratio. A sustained drop is the warm-pool-exhaustion signal — the ResumeWarmHitRateLow alert fires off this same expression.

defaults.noValue: the thaw-path resume counters recorded nothing in the selected range, so the warm-graft ratio has no denominator (thaw-warm + thaw-fresh = 0). It populates once thaw-path resumes fire. A blank panel cannot separate an idle warm path from an exporter that stopped — confirm with `up{component="slack-bridge"} == 1`.

panels.title: Interrupt/resume plumbing — pool serve rates, coop restore, salvage (C8 ka-0000000550)
Warm-B claim outcomes (hit / miss / error)
panels.description: gardenio_warm_placeholder_claims_total — every thaw-path attempt to claim a Ready warm-B placeholder, by outcome. hit = grafted onto a pre-Ready placeholder (the sub-second R4 path); miss = no Ready placeholder in the (node,topology) bucket, fell back to create-then-restore (R3); error = the claim itself failed. Complements the warm-graft hit-rate stat above, which is derived from the resume-latency histogram: this series counts attempts even when the subsequent thaw fails before recording a latency sample.

defaults.noValue: the gardenio_warm_placeholder_claims_total counter recorded nothing in the selected range (the warm-graft path is not yet exercised). Series appear once a thaw resume claims a Ready placeholder. A blank panel cannot separate that pre-traffic state from a controller exporter that stopped — confirm with `up{component="agents"} == 1` (poolmanager emits this counter from the controller process).

panels.title: Prewarmed-pool assign outcomes (hit / empty / error)
panels.description: gardenio_prewarmed_assigns_total — every Slack-thread warm fast-path assignment attempt (AssignPrewarmed), by outcome and (project,role) pool. empty = the pool had no assignable warm pod and the mention paid a cold mint; a sustained empty rate on a busy pool means MinSize is too small or refill is broken.

panels.title: coop --resume conversation-restore outcomes
panels.description: gardenio_coop_resume_attempts_total — one per coop session that requested a --resume conversation restore (the path EVERY non-runsc agent takes after an interrupt). resumed = the prior transcript was discovered/parsed and Claude relaunched with --resume; any fresh_* outcome means the conversation was NOT restored and the agent started over: fresh_no_session (no transcript / under the 256-byte stub threshold — the truncated-log shape), fresh_parse_error, fresh_discovery_error, fresh_no_uuid (transcript had no parseable session UUID). Scraped from agent pods (:9093); the counter is constant per session, and VictoriaMetrics' increase() counts each new series' initial value, so this charts new resume attempts.

panels.title: coop --resume prepare latency (max over live sessions)
panels.description: gardenio_coop_resume_prepare_seconds — wall-clock seconds a session spent preparing its restore (S3 transcript download when configured + local discovery + JSONL parse), by outcome. One gauge per live session; max/avg across sessions bounds the restore cost on the dominant resume path.

panels.title: Salvage runs by outcome (preStop WIP rescue)
panels.description: gardenio_salvage_runs_total — one per `gb salvage` preStop run that found dirty worktrees, by outcome: success (every target bundled to S3), partial (some), failed (none). Clean teardowns with nothing to rescue are not counted. Before this counter, salvage success was invisible: preStop stderr is discarded (ka-0000000550). NOTE: salvage series are pushed by gb from agent pods via the vmagent import endpoint, which does not stamp external_labels — so they carry no env label and are not filtered by $env (same as gardenio_prime_hook_bytes).

panels.title: Salvage volume — rescued bytes & worktrees
panels.description: gardenio_salvage_bytes_total (bundle bytes durably uploaded to S3) and gardenio_salvage_targets_total (dirty worktrees uploaded vs skipped). A rising skipped share means bundles are hitting the 64 MiB cap, the 25s deadline, or S3 denials — WIP is being lost on teardown. NOTE: salvage series are pushed by gb from agent pods via the vmagent import endpoint, which does not stamp external_labels — so they carry no env label and are not filtered by $env (same as gardenio_prime_hook_bytes).

panels.title: Mention cold-respawn SLO — Slack @-mention re-entry latency (GRADE 2026-07-29, ka-0000002086)
Mention cold-respawn latency p50 / p95 / p99 — SLO < 30s (p95)
panels.description: histogram_quantile over gardenio_mention_cold_respawn_seconds_bucket: the cold-respawn boot latency for thread/DM agents — wall-clock from a follow-up arriving (top of respawnThreadAgent) to the respawned agent's first proof-of-life (SessionStart hook firing, i.e. Claude booted in the container). This is the 'follow-up → first token' latency the warm-idle keepalive (ka-0000005793) is built to remove; the warm path never creates a new session here, so this is the COLD path only. The dashed threshold marks the p95 < 30s SLO: sub-30s feels responsive to a human who just @-mentioned an agent, above rides the image-pull / PVC-restore tail. Quiet windows show no line (a cold respawn is a discrete, occasional event); zoom the range if empty.

title: Gardenio — resume latency (thaw / sub-second-resume)
description: Agent resume latency by path and regime (R0–R4): thaw-warm p50/p95 against their gates, warm-graft hit rate, cold-fallback count, prewarmed-pool and warm-B claim outcomes, coop --resume restore outcomes, preStop salvage, and mention cold-respawn latency vs its 30s SLO. Open this when a respawn felt slow or a session came back cold.
